memory_update.text: CGNX should remain the reference benchmark for the industrial machine-vision lane, but not the only candidate because it is already relatively visible and above the preferred small/mid-cap discovery range.

NOVT is a promising underfollowed candidate for the edge-industrial-AI automation node because its exposure is embedded in components, machine vision, RFID, end-of-arm robotics, photonics, and metrology rather than labeled as AI.

ATS is a useful underfollowed integration-layer candidate: its relevance depends on whether custom automation backlog is tied to high-validation AI/inspection/robotics workflows rather than conventional industrial capex.

ZBRA belongs in the discovery lane despite larger market cap because its machine vision, RFID, RTLS, fixed scanning, and workflow-data assets map to the physical-AI visibility layer; robotics-exit disclosures must be monitored as a thesis risk.

Need a later layer to quantify revenue exposure by sub-node: machine vision, RFID/RTLS, metrology, robotics end-effectors, automation integration, and lifecycle service. Current Layer 1B evidence supports inclusion but not yet revenue purity.

The most investable chokepoint framing for this node is validated sensing and integration: AI deployment in physical operations needs machine vision, identification, metrology, safety, commissioning, and workflow data before model intelligence can create throughput gains.

node: Industrial and edge AI automation: sensors, machine vision, controllers, test/inspection, and robotics-enabling software
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the industrial and edge-AI automation node using a two-lane funnel. The reference lane keeps Cognex as the clearest machine-vision benchmark. The underfollowed lane emphasizes Novanta, ATS, and Zebra as second-order automation enablers across machine vision, robotic end-effectors, metrology, workflow digitization, RFID, fixed scanning, and custom factory automation. The strongest chokepoint angle is not generic AI models but validated sensing, inspection, control, metrology, and integration layers that make AI deployable in factories, warehouses, and regulated production environments. Key caveat: exposure must be verified by segment revenue, customer mix, order/backlog quality, and whether AI-enabled automation is incremental growth or merely relabeled industrial capex.
